newsitem.title: BULGARIA: WORLD BANK MAY FUND BULGARIA ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECT.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BANK MAY FUND BULGARIA ENVIRONMENTAL PROJECT.

text.p: The World Bank said on Thursday it was willing to help Bulgaria finance capacity expansion, upgrading and solving environmental problems of its copper smelter MDK-Pirdop after the company is privatised.

"The Bank's position has been and remains that it is willing to work with any suitable strategic partner(s), selected by the government, with the qualifications required to make a success of the proposed smelter upgrade," A World Bank's statement said.
The bank suggests options for helping fund the expansion and environmental imrovements at the plant.

They are "either as one component of a loan to deal with the environmental liabilities incurred as a result of past environmental damages of former state enterprises and/or via an equity investment and loans to the privatised company through the International Finance Corporation (IFC), the private sector arm of the World Bank Group," the statement said.

The bank said in August it was prepared to consider a $40-50 million loan, which was requested by the Bulgarian government in 1995 for reducing the pollution from industries and the use of leaded gasoline.

The two projects, which are in a preparation stage of the Pollution Abatement/Lead Reduction Project, involve the country's biggest oil refinery Neftohim on the Black Sea port of Bourgas and the Pirdop smelter in western Bulgaria.
Bulgaria's cabinet, eager to bring in much needed capital for its slumping economy, decided in September to sell the smelter within the next few months.
The bank said the smelter's current electrolytic refinery, producing refined copper, needed to be replaced by a much larger refinery, which requires a bigger investment.

The bank has supplied a list of 20 international companies in the non-ferrous metals industry at the request of the Bulgarian government as a strategic partner would ensure access to investment resources, technical experience and trading expertise in the world copper market, it added.
